problems.problem: Potential lead intake latency or manual data re-entry between WordPress Formidable forms and the central field-service management platform (ServiceTitan).
problems.label: hypothesis
problems.basis: The website uses Formidable Forms submitting to WordPress rather than an integrated ServiceTitan web booking widget, meaning form submissions likely route via email to dispatch.

problems.problem: Mismatched service category selections on the primary scheduling form ('Air Conditioning' and 'Heating' on a plumbing site) causing misrouted or unqualified triage.
problems.label: inference

problems.problem: Incomplete attribution or reporting latency across multi-channel paid ad sources (Google Ads, Bing Ads, Facebook, Choozle) and booked revenue in ServiceTitan.
problems.label: hypothesis
problems.basis: Active presence of multiple ad platforms and ClickCease click protection suggests significant marketing spend, where cross-platform cost-per-booked-job reporting often requires manual aggregation.

existingSolutions.addresses: Directly injects customer booking requests into ServiceTitan scheduling dispatch with live availability and automatic customer profile creation.
Automatically triggers an API payload from WordPress form submissions to external CRMs or ServiceTitan Booking API.
Tracks revenue attribution by campaign and integrates ad spend reporting with dispatch outcomes.

forgexSolutions.name: Revenue Leak Check
forgexSolutions.description: A one-week operational diagnostic auditing web form response speeds, off-hours dispatch handling, call attribution, and missed inquiries against booked jobs.
forgexSolutions.problem: Unverified lead drop-off between paid advertising clicks, website form submissions, and actual dispatch board booking.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: ServiceTitan and Google Analytics track activity within their own silos but do not benchmark end-to-end response lag or measure off-hours leakage without independent auditing.

forgexSolutions.name: Lead-to-job pipeline
forgexSolutions.description: Integration bridge connecting website Formidable booking forms directly to ServiceTitan's Booking API within two minutes, with automated customer confirmation SMS.
forgexSolutions.problem: Forms currently route to WordPress/dispatch email, risking manual transcription delay during peak call periods or overnight.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: While ServiceTitan provides an off-the-shelf booking widget, contractors often prefer custom on-brand forms that require lightweight middleware to post cleanly into ServiceTitan.

forgexSolutions.name: Owner's Monday numbers
forgexSolutions.description: Single-page weekly dashboard compiling booked plumbing revenue, average ticket, ad spend, and cost per booked call across ServiceTitan, ad networks, and QuickBooks.
forgexSolutions.problem: Disparate reporting across Choozle, ClickCease, Google Ads, and ServiceTitan complicates weekly commercial visibility.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: Standard platform dashboards do not unify third-party ad network spend, accounting data, and field job completion in one simple Monday executive report.

feasibility.explanation: The company's digital stack uses standard WordPress architecture with Formidable Forms alongside ServiceTitan infrastructure, both of which support webhooks and REST APIs for automated data synchronization.

aiDelivery.explanation: AI models can handle conversational triage, inquiry categorization, and draft dispatch replies, but core lead pipeline synchronization and dashboard aggregation rely on deterministic API connectors.

humanReview: Dispatchers must review and confirm technician job assignments before finalizing appointments on the calendar.
Emergency service inquiries submitted after-hours require immediate dispatcher telephone verification.
Weekly executive metrics must be reconciled against certified bank and accounting statements.

risks.description: Automated form routing must not bypass on-call emergency dispatch protocols for urgent situations like flooding or ruptured water lines.
SMS notifications to customers submitting booking requests must strictly honor TCPA consent checkboxes already implemented on the site forms.
API keys connecting WordPress form endpoints to ServiceTitan or reporting databases must be secured against unauthorized access.

commercial.implementationCost: $1,800 setup plus $149/month for Lead-to-job pipeline, or $500 for Revenue Leak Check
assumptions: Plumbing Solutions of Idaho advertises standard drain cleaning jobs costing between $100 and $300 (average midpoint $200).

If lead intake delays or missed follow-ups cause 3 to 5 standard drain cleaning jobs ($200 each) to slip through per month, illustrative lost gross revenue is $600 to $1,000 monthly ($7,200 to $12,000 annually).
Value will be higher if larger repairs or installations (such as water heaters or repiping) are delayed or lost.

questions: When a customer submits a service request on your schedule page, how does that inquiry currently enter ServiceTitan—via direct API, email alert to dispatch, or manual entry?
How do your on-call dispatchers handle after-hours or weekend web form submissions for emergency plumbing calls?
How do you currently track marketing spend efficiency across Google Ads, Choozle, and other channels down to completed jobs in ServiceTitan?
discovery.outreachSubject: Service scheduling workflow / Plumbing Solutions of Idaho
discovery.outreachBody:
Hi [Owner / General Manager Name],

My name is [Founder Name] with ForgeX. We work with established plumbing and home-service trade contractors to streamline lead intake and field-service integration.

While reviewing your website, I noticed your online service scheduling page uses a custom WordPress form that appears to route to your dispatch email, even though your site references ServiceTitan assets. In many plumbing operations, web submissions can take valuable minutes to get transcribed into ServiceTitan, especially during morning dispatch rushes or overnight emergency calls.

We don't sell generic software and don't make promises without understanding your specific workflow. If you or your dispatch team ever find that web inquiries or after-hours requests create unnecessary transcription work, I'd welcome the chance to share how similar plumbing contractors bridge that pipeline automatically.

If you prefer not to hear from us, simply reply with 'opt out' or 'remove' and I will respect your preference immediately.

Best regards,

[Founder Name]
Founder, ForgeX
[Founder Street Address, City, State, ZIP]
[Founder Phone Number] | [Founder Email]

limitations: No individual owner, executive, or manager names are listed on the public website.
Internal dispatch workflows and whether Formidable Forms connects to ServiceTitan via backend webhooks cannot be definitively confirmed from public frontend inspection.
State licensing registry records were not independently inspected beyond the contractor license number published on site.

qualification.rationale: Plumbing Solutions of Idaho fits ForgeX's target profile: an established owner-led plumbing contractor in Meridian, ID with ~10 to 75 personnel, active paid advertising (Google Ads, Bing Ads, Choozle, ClickCease), and field-service software (ServiceTitan). Observable operational surfaces exist—such as web booking through WordPress Formidable Forms rather than ServiceTitan's live booking widget, and mismatched HVAC options on their booking form. However, because public website analysis cannot verify whether their dispatch team experiences delays or already utilizes custom webhook automation into ServiceTitan, the operational problems remain hypotheses. The account should be pursued later via founder discovery questions.
